title: FlickerTalk plugin manifest
description: What module.json says about a plugin. The app reads it only after the catalogue's signature checks out (Plan §49–§50).

id.description: Reverse domain name, lowercase; the folder the plugin is served from.

minCoreVersion.description: The oldest FlickerTalk this plugin runs on (§51).

components.description: The web components it registers; the first one is what the app shows.

kind.description: What it is to the user (2026-10-02): a tool, opened from the chat, "open with" or as a viewer; or a game, opened from the games with a contact. A tool unless it says otherwise. A game may ask only for live and send, and opens no file; it needs minCoreVersion 1.3.0 or newer to be published.

summary.description: One line about what it does, for the catalogue. In English.

icon.description: The name of an Ionicon (outline style, e.g. image-outline) the app shows for this plugin in its Apps grid and sheets (2026-10-08). Without it the app shows a generic tool or game icon.

locales.description: The name and the summary in other languages (2026-10-02), by the app's language code: es, pt, fr, de, it, ro, ru, uk, pl, tr, ar, hi, bn, id, vi, th, ja, ko, zh-CN, zh-TW. The app (from 1.3.0) shows the one of its language, then of its base language (zh for zh-TW), and the English top-level name and summary otherwise. A code the app does not speak is never shown. English is the top level, so there is no en.

views.description: The kinds of file it is the viewer of (2026-09-27): exact media types only, each also in opens. A tap on such a file in the chat opens it here without the user choosing, so a viewer may not ask for network.

opens.description: The kinds of file it opens (2026-09-27): media types like image/png, image/* or */* for any. The app offers "open with" for a message whose file matches, and the plugin gets the bytes in onOpen.

permissions.description: What it asks the user for. Installing grants none of it (§53).

network.description: Hosts it may reach, never wildcards or URLs. The core checks every call against this (§55).

messages.description: Whether it may read the message or text the user hands it. It never reads more.

send.description: How far it goes when it writes in the chat: not at all, it fills the composer, or it sends.

print.description: Whether it may ask the phone to print what it made. The user picks the printer.

live.description: Whether it may talk to the same plugin on the other side of a conversation, over the direct connection, encrypted; never through a server (2026-09-27).

remind.description: Whether it may set reminders: a notification on this phone at a time it picks (2026-09-27).

drive.description: Whether it may keep files in the user's own cloud through the core's vault, encrypted on the phone (2026-09-27).

storage.description: How much it may keep in its records: small (4 MB, the default) or large (256 MB) (2026-09-27).

location.description: Whether it may ask for the phone's current position, once, while the app is open; the phone asks the user the first time (2026-10-02).
